Definition: a strengthened form of a simpler primary θάνω (which is used for it only in certain tenses); to die (literally or figuratively):--be dead, die.
BiblicalUsage: thnḗskō is the word for to die. In Matthew 2:20, Saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and it appears again in Luke 7:12. In the Greek text the word is spelled θνῄσκω.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that death is real and terrible, and it is also the enemy Christ has already faced.
